label: prf:dq-squared
title: Proof of $d_q^2$ does not vanish
html:
Write a = q^{-1} and b = 1 - q^{-1}, so a + b = 1. Then

\begin{align*}
  d_q^2\alpha
  &= d_q\bigl(ad\alpha + b\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha\bigr) \\
  &= a^2d^2\alpha
     + abd(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha)
     + ab\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_{\xi}d\alpha
     + b^2\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha).
\end{align*}

The first term vanishes since d^2 = 0. The second expands as abd\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha - ab\varTheta \wedge d\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. The third term cancels the second's negative part because [d, \mathcal{L}_\xi] = 0 implies \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_{\xi}d\alpha = \varTheta \wedge d\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. For the fourth term, the Reeb field satisfies \mathcal{L}_\xi\varTheta = 0 (since \iota_\xi d\varTheta = 0 and \varTheta(\xi)=1), so \mathcal{L}_\xi(\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha) = \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi^2\alpha; the factor \varTheta \wedge \varTheta = 0 in b^2\varTheta \wedge \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi^2\alpha kills this term. Hence d_q^2\alpha = abd\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha.
